headline: A Springer Nature journal retracted a review of AI in communication research because its own text appears to have been written with undeclared AI.
score_reason: One retraction with an official notice, telling as an example of the citation fingerprint of machine-written papers, but a single case with no wider action announced.
importance_line: Researchers who lean on review articles lose a reference that stood for two years, journals get a clear example of how mismatched citations expose undeclared AI writing, and one author contests the decision, so the account of how the paper was produced stays disputed.
summary: Scienmag reports, in a text carried by Bioengineer.org, that Discover Artificial Intelligence, a Springer Nature journal, published a retraction note on 3 Oct 2026 withdrawing a May 2024 critical review by two Hunan Normal University authors on AI in communication research, after finding a number of citations that did not fit their context, a pattern the publisher said may suggest undeclared use of generative AI. Springer Nature said the authors gave no satisfactory explanation and it no longer trusts the article; one author, Muhammad Asif, disagrees with the retraction and the other did not respond.
notes: Source corrected from Bioengineer.org (copy site) to Scienmag, which wrote the text; URL is the Scienmag original named in the article.
